title: An unanswered question parks the stream open rather than closing it
rationale: THE TERMINAL-CLOSE RULE IS KEYED ON TERMINAL STATES ONLY. TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED is not one, so the stream must stay OPEN and must report itself as interrupted. This vector exists to stop a second implementer from 'tidying up' by closing the stream on a non-terminal state: a close there is indistinguishable client-side from a dropped connection, and the client cannot tell whether to answer the question, retry, or re-subscribe. Keeping it open also means the answer's effects arrive on the connection the client is already reading. A serving layer bounds the wait with its own deadline and, on expiry, drives the task to a REAL terminal state so the ordinary close rule ends the stream — it never hangs up silently.
